name: muon

phase_0.boundary_condition: The electroweak vacuum and conservation laws (charge, lepton flavor, energy-momentum) that define the muon's allowed interactions and decay channels

⊢.justification: The uninitialized quantum field configuration before the muon field excitation is created

⊣.justification: The closed boundary containing the complete decay products where all conserved quantities are balanced

≻.justification: Forward morphism representing the muon's worldline evolution between creation and decay vertices

≺.justification: Contravariant morphism for the CPT-conjugate process (antimuon decay) or virtual exchange reversal

⋈.chosen_element: sequential vertex composition in Feynman diagrams
⋈.justification: Composition of gauge interaction vertices (photon, W, Z couplings) along the muon line

⊙.chosen_element: muon self-identity via lepton flavor number
⊙.justification: Self-reference through the conserved muon number that distinguishes it from electron and tau

∈.justification: The muon's quantum state splits into decay arm (weak vertex) and persistence arm (propagation), reflecting its finite lifetime

∋.justification: Rejoining of the decay arms into the final three-particle state where flavor and charge are conserved

⊤.justification: Affirmative arm: the W⁻ emission vertex actually occurs, producing the decay products

⊥.justification: Negative arm: the muon continues propagating without weak interaction at this proper time step

⊞.justification: Paradice state: the muon simultaneously holds decay amplitude and propagation amplitude in the quantum superposition before measurement

⊡.justification: Irreversible fixation of the decay vertex in a detector, creating a permanent classical record

phase_2.split_input: muon quantum state at a given proper time
phase_2.fuse_result: final state (e⁻ + ν̄ₑ + ν_μ) with conserved charge and lepton flavors
phase_2.failure_reason: FSPLIT3 at step 5 dangles — no matching FFUSE3

phase_3.void_description: No muon field excitation present; vacuum before pair production or cosmic ray shower
phase_3.true_description: Decay vertex confirmed: muon has transformed to electron plus neutrinos with all conservation laws satisfied
phase_3.false_description: Muon persists without decay at this proper time interval; flavor number unchanged
phase_3.both_description: Quantum superposition of decayed and undecayed amplitudes during the muon's lifetime, holding both flavor-change and flavor-preservation simultaneously

steps.domain_action: Initialize the muon field excitation from vacuum via pair production or cosmic ray interaction
Establish muon self-identity through muon lepton flavor number (L_μ = +1)
Propagate muon forward along worldline through electromagnetic field interactions
Compose sequential QED vertices (photon couplings) during propagation
Open metastable decay fork — split into decay arm (weak interaction) and persistence arm (continued propagation)
On decay arm — realize W⁻ emission vertex (μ⁻ → W⁻ + ν_μ), affirmative weak interaction
On decay arm — propagate virtual W⁻ forward to its decay vertex
On decay arm — split W⁻ decay into electron arm (W⁻ → e⁻ + ν̄ₑ) and alternative hadronic arms (suppressed)
On electron arm — realize leptonic W⁻ decay vertex, affirmative
On hadronic arms — suppress hadronic channels (kinematically forbidden for real W at this mass), negative
Rejoin W⁻ decay arms into leptonic final state (e⁻ + ν̄ₑ) — dominant branch wins
Compose muon decay vertex with W⁻ decay vertex into full decay chain
Apply CPT conjugation to generate antimuon decay amplitude (μ⁺ → e⁺ + νₑ + ν̄_μ)
Verify antimuon carries opposite lepton flavor (L_μ = -1) and charge (+1)
Open fork for antimuon decay vs persistence (mirror of muon fork)
On antimuon decay arm — realize W⁺ emission vertex
On antimuon decay arm — propagate virtual W⁺ to decay
Split W⁺ decay into positron arm and hadronic arms
On positron arm — realize leptonic W⁺ decay
On hadronic arms — suppress
Rejoin antimuon decay arms
Compose antimuon decay chain
Hold muon/antimuon decay superposition in quantum field theory (both amplitudes live in path integral)
Fix decay event in detector — irreversible measurement record (track, calorimeter deposit, timing)
Close at final state — electron/positron plus neutrinos with all quantum numbers balanced

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Standard Model Lagrangian — translates particle quantum numbers into allowed vertices and Feynman rules
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Quantum field state space (Fock space) — stores particle number, momentum, spin, flavor quantum numbers
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Proper time evolution along worldline — orders vertices by invariant time; decay probability per unit time Γ = 1/τ
phase_5.alfs_store: Particle Data Group (PDG) review — canonical reference for muon mass, lifetime, branching ratios, couplings

phase_6.cycle_cost: One unit of muon rest mass energy (105.66 MeV) released as kinetic energy of decay products per decay cycle
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Single muon at rest (or in motion) with definite flavor, charge, spin; low entropy pure quantum state
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Three-body final state (e⁻ + ν̄ₑ + ν_μ) with distributed momenta and spins; higher entropy due to phase space volume
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS > 0 — Decay increases entropy by converting a single massive particle into three lighter particles with large phase space; the weak interaction vertex is the entropy-producing step

⊣=𐑡: The muon participates in electroweak and gravitational interactions as a node in the Standard Model's particle interaction network, connecting to gauge bosons and other leptons through fundamental force vertices without hierarchical containment or cyclic closure.
⊢=𐑼: The muon operates as a point-like particle in quantum field theory, with its interactions localized to vertices in Feynman diagrams and no intrinsic spatial extension or iterative temporal cycling defining its fundamental behavior.
⊞=𐑳: The muon participates in interactions with asymmetric participation ratios, such as coupling to a single W boson in weak decay or pairing with one antimuon in annihilation, rather than forming symmetric pairs or higher-order oligomers.
⊡=𐑴: The muon carries a conserved lepton flavor number (muon number) that cannot change continuously and requires a discrete weak interaction vertex to violate, making its role Z2-protected against continuous deformation to a trivial state.
⊙=𐑢: The muon exists as a stable massive particle in the normal vacuum regime without exhibiting scale-free correlations or critical fluctuations, operating well below any phase transition threshold in its standard environment.
⊥=𐑖: The muon exhibits persistent chirality through its intrinsic spin-1/2 and weak isospin structure, where left-handed and right-handed components couple differently to the electroweak force, creating structurally enforced symmetry breaking across multiple interaction axes that cannot be thermally interconverted.
≻=𐑑: The muon undergoes irreversible weak decay into an electron and neutrinos via W boson exchange, a structural transformation that changes particle identity and lepton flavor rather than a reversible association or catalytic process.
≺=𐑿: The muon carries a definite negative electric charge (−1) and muon lepton number (+1), creating a signed directional interface where it acts as a source for electromagnetic fields and a donor of lepton flavor in weak interactions, with its antiparticle (antimuon) providing the opposite signed poles.
⋈=𐑐: The muon's weak and electromagnetic interactions are governed by precise gauge couplings and conservation laws that enforce deterministic vertex rules in Feynman diagrams, yielding near-certain interaction outcomes when kinematically allowed.
⊤=𐑪: The muon is a metastable particle with a finite lifetime (2.2 μs) that cannot decay to its ground state (electron) without the extraordinary perturbation of a weak interaction vertex, remaining kinetically locked in a non-ground-state configuration.
∈=𐑲: The muon's fundamental interactions occur at localized vertices in spacetime (point-like gauge couplings), with no intrinsic correlation length extending beyond the immediate interaction event itself.
∋=𐑠: The muon engages partners sequentially in its weak decay chain (muon → W⁻ + ν_μ, then W⁻ → e⁻ + ν̄_e), requiring ordered steps rather than simultaneous or alternative partner selection.
